findings.highlight: It's too late to regret it now.
findings.evidenceJa: 今さらシンパシーを感じても遅すぎるってのに。
findings.explanation: シンパシー, belatedly feeling sympathy or kinship with Kazusa, becomes generic regret.
findings.japanese: 今さらシンパシーを感じても遅すぎるってのに。
findings.todokanai: It's too late to regret it now.

findings.highlight: Touma isn't all too opposed to the idea of just forgetting about what happened
findings.evidenceJa: 全部帳消しにしてもいいような気もしないでもなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that Kazusa's present expression almost makes him feel that he could let everything be wiped clean. The English transfers that willingness to Kazusa, making her the person who may be ready to forget what happened.
findings.japanese:
なんとなく、今の冬馬の表情で、
全部帳消しにしてもいいような気もしないでもなかった。
findings.todokanai: Judging by her expression, I get the feeling Touma isn't all too opposed to the idea of just forgetting about what happened.

findings.highlight: any chance of explaining myself in a cool-headed manner is out the window
findings.evidenceJa: 真面目と自己弁護するには虚しすぎる
findings.explanation: After admitting how much he enjoyed Setsuna's touch, Haruki says it would be too hollow to defend his reaction as mere earnestness or propriety. The English instead says he has lost the ability to explain himself cool-headedly, replacing the moral self-indictment with a claim about composure.
findings.japanese:
思わず小木曽の手の届かない頭上へと両手を掲げ、
至福の感触を放棄してしまう俺は、
真面目と自己弁護するには虚しすぎる。
findings.todokanai: I instinctively raise my hands above my head so Ogiso can't reach them, relinquishing myself of the blissful sensation of her hands. With that, any chance of explaining myself in a cool-headed manner is out the window.

findings.highlight: I'd never seen her until last year
findings.evidenceJa: 去年まで全然見かけなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had never seen Kazusa through the end of last year, consistent with her move into the regular curriculum this year. The English says he first saw her last year, shifting the timeline by a year.
findings.japanese:
「でも、ま、
道理で去年まで全然見かけなかったわけだ」
findings.todokanai: "Well, in that case, it's no wonder I'd never seen her until last year."

findings.highlight: were without a doubt from that 21
findings.evidenceJa: 全２１人中何番目くらいだったんだろう
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders what rank, among the twenty-one girls, Takeya's attempted introductions would have occupied. The English merely says those girls were among the twenty-one, deleting the ranking punchline and replacing the question with a certainty.
findings.japanese:
今まで俺に紹介してくれようとした女の子たちは、
全２１人中何番目くらいだったんだろう…
findings.todokanai: All the girls he's been trying to introduce me to were without a doubt from that 21…

findings.highlight: a model student ever since she enrolled in the music program
findings.evidenceJa: 音楽科始まって以来の優等生
findings.explanation: The claim is that Kazusa was an outstanding student in the history of the music program—since the program itself began—not merely that she behaved as a model student from the date of her own enrollment. The same phrase is translated correctly at ref 240, making the local error especially clear.
findings.japanese:
「冬馬かずさはな…
入学当時、音楽科始まって以来の優等生だったんだとよ」
findings.todokanai: "Touma Kazusa, you see… was a model student ever since she enrolled in the music program."

findings.highlight: At first, the music teachers had all praised Touma. When compared to Touma, her classmates all appeared to be inexperienced amateurs.
findings.evidenceJa:
当初、音楽科の教師たちはこぞって冬馬を持ち上げ、
クラスメートたちは彼女と比較され、
その未熟さを幾度となくこき下ろされたらしい。
findings.explanation: Teachers repeatedly disparaging the other students as immature by comparison is reduced to classmates merely appearing inexperienced.
findings.japanese:
当初、音楽科の教師たちはこぞって冬馬を持ち上げ、
クラスメートたちは彼女と比較され、
その未熟さを幾度となくこき下ろされたらしい。
findings.todokanai: At first, the music teachers had all praised Touma. When compared to Touma, her classmates all appeared to be inexperienced amateurs.

findings.highlight: grit their teeth while taking all the jobs others wouldn't want to do
findings.evidenceJa: 他人の嫌がる仕事を黙らずにやる
findings.explanation: Haruki characterizes the class representative's role as doing the work others hate without keeping quiet about it—a pointed description of his own competent but vocal interventionism. 'Grit their teeth' implies silent endurance and reverses the 黙らず qualification.
findings.japanese:
他人の嫌がる仕事を黙らずにやるのが
クラス委員の仕事じゃなかったのか？
findings.todokanai: Isn't it the representative's job to grit their teeth while taking all the jobs others wouldn't want to do?

findings.highlight: She might refuse, despite getting along with you
findings.evidenceJa: 仲間とつるむのに拒否反応があるかもしれない
findings.explanation: Takeya warns that Kazusa may have an aversive reaction to associating with a group at all. The English presupposes that she already gets along with Haruki and merely may refuse his request, changing both the social diagnosis and the warning.
findings.japanese:
「難しいぞ、あのコは。
仲間とつるむのに拒否反応があるかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "She's going to be a difficult one, that girl. She might refuse, despite getting along with you."

findings.highlight: On top of that, it's because… she's the one who played that beautiful melody…
findings.evidenceJa: しかも、その音を奏でてたのが…だったのなら…
findings.explanation: Haruki's suspended counterfactual—if the person producing that sound was...—is completed and supplied with the unsupported phrase 'beautiful melody.'
findings.japanese: しかも、その音を奏でてたのが…だったのなら…
findings.todokanai: On top of that, it's because… she's the one who played that beautiful melody…

findings.highlight: there are also times when you should really take a step back
findings.evidenceJa: お前は気を使ってるつもりで、実は一歩も退かなかったりする
findings.explanation: Takeya's point is not generic advice to step back: Haruki believes he is being considerate while in fact sometimes refusing to yield even a single step. The English deletes that gap between Haruki's self-image and behavior, immediately relevant to the confrontation that follows.
findings.japanese:
「あと、いつもみたいな説教もやめとけ。
お前は気を使ってるつもりで、
実は一歩も退かなかったりすることがあるからな」
findings.todokanai: "Also, don't go off lecturing like you always do. I know you mean well, but there are also times when you should really take a step back."

findings.highlight: I can hear nothing off-key. I can't clearly hear every note
findings.evidenceJa: 音が跳んでるところが見つからない。あまり聴く機会はないけど、プロと区別がつかない
findings.explanation: Haruki's amateur ears cannot find any skipped notes, and although he rarely has occasion to hear professionals, he cannot distinguish Kazusa from one. The English changes missing notes into bad intonation and misreads his limited exposure to professionals as an inability to hear every note.
findings.japanese:
素人耳では、音が跳んでるところが見つからない。
あまり聴く機会はないけど、プロと区別がつかない。
…まぁ、だからこそ素人なんだけど。
findings.todokanai: Being the amateur I am, I can hear nothing off-key. I can't clearly hear every note, but I can't tell her apart from a professional… Well, I guess that's what makes me an amateur.

findings.highlight: if I keep on rambling anyway
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がしつこく話しかけても気にするな
findings.explanation: Haruki tells Kazusa not to mind when he persistently approaches and talks to her, claiming the future right to keep initiating contact despite her silence. 'Rambling' instead describes the manner or length of speech within a conversation and loses the relationship-forming persistence.
findings.japanese:
「だから冬馬も、
俺がしつこく話しかけても気にするな」
findings.todokanai: "So please don't hold it against me if I keep on rambling anyway, Touma."

findings.highlight: I know all about how you've spent the past two years
findings.evidenceJa: 二年間、冬馬がどんな思いで過ごしてきたか
findings.explanation: Haruki provocatively claims to know what feelings Kazusa has lived with for two years. The English makes this sound like factual knowledge of how she spent the period, suppressing the invasive psychological certainty that angers her.
findings.japanese:
「だからさ、今の俺には全部わかってるんだ。
二年間、冬馬がどんな思いで過ごしてきたかってこと」
findings.todokanai: "Like I said, I understand everything now. I know all about how you've spent the past two years."

findings.highlight: I think you should try to get along with everyone
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬は、皆に歩み寄るべきだったと思う
findings.explanation: Haruki judges that Kazusa should have met the others halfway during the preceding two years. The English turns that retrospective judgment into mild present-tense advice to get along with everyone, reducing both its severity and its relevance to the history he is prosecuting.
findings.japanese:
「だけどさ、厳しいこと言ってるかもしれないけど、
それでも冬馬は、皆に歩み寄るべきだったと思うんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Still, you know… although this may sound quite painful, I think you should try to get along with everyone."

findings.highlight: I'm not sure if people our age would understand such a line of thought
findings.evidenceJa: 俺らの歳でこんな悟ったようなこと言ってもしょうがない
findings.explanation: Haruki undercuts himself, saying there is little point in someone their age talking as though he were enlightened. The English instead suggests that their peers may be unable to understand his insight, reversing self-mockery into intellectual superiority.
findings.japanese:
「そんな生き方の方が今よりよっぽど楽しいと思うけどな。
いや、まぁ俺らの歳でこんな悟ったようなこと言っても
しょうがないとは思うんだけど」
findings.todokanai: "I think living that way is a lot better in comparison. No, I guess I'm not sure if people our age would understand such a line of thought."

findings.highlight: you and us guitarists
findings.evidenceJa: 小木曽以外にはギターしかいない
findings.explanation: Haruki admits that besides Setsuna there is only a guitar—that is, Haruki himself—in the club. The plural 'us guitarists' invents at least one additional guitarist and obscures how radically incomplete the band remains.
findings.japanese:
「だからその…
キーボードがいるみたいに嘘ついてたこと。
本当は、小木曽以外にはギターしかいないのに」
findings.todokanai: "Well, you know… at me for lying that we had a keyboardist. There really isn't anyone else other than you and us guitarists."

findings.highlight: that miracle of a session on that day was only made possible
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬のピアノと小木曽の歌声が合わさったとき、あの日の奇跡のセッションが、やっと完成する
findings.explanation: Haruki looks forward: when Kazusa's piano and Setsuna's voice come together, the miraculous session from that day will finally become complete. The English converts this goal into a past causal statement about what had already made the earlier session possible, erasing the imagined completion of the trio.
findings.japanese:
俺のギターはともかく、
冬馬のピアノと小木曽の歌声が合わさったとき、
あの日の奇跡のセッションが、やっと完成するんだから。
findings.todokanai: Putting aside my performance, that miracle of a session on that day was only made possible by both Touma's piano and Ogiso's singing.

findings.highlight: it most likely had something to do with my attitude
findings.evidenceJa: 純粋に、俺の態度に対してのものだった
findings.explanation: Although Haruki still does not know why, he concludes that Kazusa's anger was directed purely at his attitude. The English reduces that explicit deduction to weak probability, weakening the premise for his plan to have someone else negotiate.
findings.japanese:
あいつが怒っているのは、
原因がさっぱりわからないというのは置いておくとして、
純粋に、俺の態度に対してのものだった。
findings.todokanai: As for why she got mad, I still don't have a clue, but it most likely had something to do with my attitude.

findings.highlight: shameless enough to tangle her up just a little bit
findings.evidenceJa: 比較的身勝手な理屈をこねるくらいには、ちょっとだけ恥知らず
findings.explanation: Haruki's narration calibrates its own moral judgment: he is shameless enough to construct a relatively selfish argument. The English invents the action of 'tangling her up' and deletes the comic self-correction over how selfish and shameless he is.
findings.japanese:
…けれど、
比較的身勝手な理屈をこねるくらいには、
ちょっとだけ恥知らずだったりする。
findings.todokanai: …However, I am shameless enough to tangle her up just a little bit.

findings.highlight: isn't it only natural for us two to know about each other
findings.evidenceJa: お互いのこと知っておくべきなのは当然だよね
findings.explanation: Setsuna throws Haruki's claim about future bandmates back at him to demand why he knows Kazusa so well; お互い refers to Haruki and Kazusa. In direct English, 'us two' refers to Setsuna and Haruki, misdirecting the retort to the people currently speaking.
findings.japanese:
「これから一緒にやっていく仲間なんだから、
お互いのこと知っておくべきなのは当然だよね？」
findings.todokanai: "We'll be doing this together, so isn't it only natural for us two to know about each other?"

findings.highlight: even a little amount of practice should be enough if you do it seriously
findings.evidenceJa: 短い期間でも本気で練習すればこれくらいできる
findings.explanation: Kazusa says this much is achievable through serious practice even over a short period. The English says only a small amount of practice is needed, contradicting the ten-hours-a-day standard she has just invoked and changing her accusation about Haruki's lack of effort.
findings.japanese:
「短い期間でも本気で練習すればこれくらいできる。
あんた偉そうなこと言ってるけど努力不足」
findings.todokanai: "To learn this, even a little amount of practice should be enough if you do it seriously. You act all high and mighty, but you don't try hard enough."

findings.highlight: help her have a more positive outlook on life
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女がそれで前向きになってくれるなら
findings.explanation: Setsuna means that the disclosure may make Kazusa more positive or receptive toward the present proposal. The English inflates that bounded hope into reforming Kazusa's entire outlook on life, changing Setsuna's immediate motive into a global judgment of her.
findings.japanese:
「うん…
彼女がそれで前向きになってくれるなら」
findings.todokanai: "Yup… If that's what would help her have a more positive outlook on life."

findings.highlight: I really want to get to know her after all you told me
findings.evidenceJa: 早くあの人と友達になりたいな
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly says she wants to become Kazusa's friend soon. The English weakens friendship to getting acquainted and invents 'after all you told me' as the cause, altering both the intimacy and urgency of her aim.
findings.japanese:
「その代わり…
絶対に、冬馬さんをわたしの前に連れてくること。
わたし、早くあの人と友達になりたいな」
findings.todokanai: "In return… I want you to get Touma-san to meet me. I really want to get to know her after all you told me."

findings.highlight: when I first heard her singing on the rooftop
findings.evidenceJa: 最初に屋上で歌ってるとこ見たとき
findings.explanation: Haruki says that when he first saw Setsuna singing on the rooftop, she struck him as someone who makes a picture. The English changes seeing to hearing, making the ensuing visual judgment 'picture perfect' lose its perceptual basis; ref 650 makes the same substitution.
findings.japanese:
「けど、本質はそんなとこじゃないんだ。
最初に屋上で歌ってるとこ見たときに感じたんだけど、
えっと、陳腐な言い方すれば『絵になる』って言うか」
findings.todokanai: "Still, that isn't really the main point here. I truly felt it when I first heard her singing on the rooftop… Well, what was that cliche phrase again? 'Picture perfect'?"

findings.highlight: I have to give up the negotiations in Music Room 2
findings.evidenceJa: 第二音楽室でのやり取りは割愛する
findings.explanation: The narrator says he will omit recounting the exchange in Music Room 2. The English says he gives up the negotiations themselves, even though the next line separately reports that the persuasion failed.
findings.japanese: まぁ、第二音楽室でのやり取りは割愛するとして。
findings.todokanai: Well, it pains me to admit it, but for now I have to give up the negotiations in Music Room 2.

findings.highlight: beautiful people are really persuasive when they're angry
findings.evidenceJa: 綺麗な人が怒ると迫力ある
findings.explanation: Setsuna says beautiful people have intimidating force or presence when angry, explaining how Kazusa drove the men away. 'Persuasive' makes the men seem convinced by an argument rather than cowed by her anger.
findings.japanese:
「しかも、みんなあっさり追い払っちゃうし。
やっぱり綺麗な人が怒ると迫力あるよねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "On top of that, you drove everyone away real quick. I guess beautiful people are really persuasive when they're angry."

findings.highlight: I don't care.
findings.evidenceJa: 知らないって
findings.explanation: Kazusa says 'I don't know,' denying Setsuna's assertion that she already understands Haruki. The English turns denial of knowledge into a declaration of indifference, changing both her stance and the setup for the repeated correction at ref 737.
findings.japanese: 「知らないって」
findings.todokanai: "I don't care."

findings.highlight: I told you, I don't care.
findings.evidenceJa: だから知らないって言ってる
findings.explanation: Kazusa repeats 'I'm telling you, I don't know,' as Setsuna presses her supposed knowledge of Haruki. Repeating 'I don't care' instead sustains the wrong emotional posture and breaks the scene's insistence on whether Kazusa knows him.
findings.japanese: 「だから知らないって言ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I told you, I don't care."

findings.highlight: You've really bought into that idiot
findings.evidenceJa: 随分と、あの馬鹿を買ってるんだな
findings.explanation: 買ってる means Setsuna values or thinks highly of Haruki. 'Bought into' instead suggests that she has accepted his pitch or been taken in by him, changing Kazusa's observation about Setsuna's esteem into skepticism about Haruki's influence.
findings.japanese: 「随分と、あの馬鹿を買ってるんだな」
findings.todokanai: "You've really bought into that idiot, huh."

findings.highlight: He kept on speaking so highly about you
findings.evidenceJa: あなたののろけ話、散々聞かされて
findings.explanation: Setsuna provocatively calls Haruki's extensive talk about Kazusa のろけ話—lovestruck or romantic boasting about her. Generic praise removes the romantic framing that makes Kazusa angry and that Haruki belatedly realizes sounded compromising.
findings.japanese:
「だぁって、わたしも怒れて来ちゃったもん。
あなたののろけ話、散々聞かされて」
findings.todokanai: "I mean, I got really angry too. He kept on speaking so highly about you."

findings.highlight: Part of the reason was probably for my sake
findings.evidenceJa: 多分、半分以上は俺のために
findings.explanation: Haruki estimates that more than half of Setsuna's ready action was probably for his sake. 'Part of the reason' removes that explicit majority and materially weakens his recognition of how strongly she is acting for him.
findings.japanese:
そして、あっさり動いてくれたから。
多分、半分以上は俺のために。
findings.todokanai: In the end, she took immediate action. Part of the reason was probably for my sake.

findings.highlight: I just dug my own grave
findings.evidenceJa: 捨てたカードが全部手札に戻ってきてしまった
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines every card he discarded as a defense returning to his hand as Setsuna quotes his own praise back at him. The generic grave idiom deletes the extended card-play logic and the joke that his supposedly discarded statements have become live evidence.
findings.japanese: 捨てたカードが全部手札に戻ってきてしまった…
findings.todokanai: Damn, I just dug my own grave…

findings.highlight: I'm not quite satisfied with the reason
findings.evidenceJa: 理由はいまいち釈然としない
findings.explanation: Haruki says the reason still is not entirely clear to him. The English says he is dissatisfied with it, changing his continuing obliviousness into a judgment that Setsuna's anger is inadequately justified.
findings.japanese: 「理由はいまいち釈然としないけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Though I'm not quite satisfied with the reason…"

findings.highlight: I made it within five minutes
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は５分くらい平気だけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says he personally does not mind Setsuna being about five minutes late, then asks whether Kazusa has anything to say. The English instead boasts that Haruki arrived within five minutes, changing who is being evaluated and removing his contrast with Kazusa's strict punctuality.
findings.japanese:
「俺は５分くらい平気だけど…
冬馬、そっちは何か言うことはないのか？」
findings.todokanai: "I made it within five minutes but… Touma, don't you have anything to say to her?"

findings.highlight: when the topic shifts to Ogiso
findings.evidenceJa: 相手が小木曽だと、途端に萎縮する
findings.explanation: Kazusa shrinks or becomes intimidated when the person she is dealing with is Setsuna. The English says her attitude changes when Setsuna becomes the topic, misidentifying direct interpersonal pressure as a conversational subject change.
findings.japanese:
相手が小木曽だと、
途端に萎縮するんだよな…何故だ？
findings.todokanai: Her attitude suddenly changes when the topic shifts to Ogiso… But seriously, why?

findings.highlight: 40 minutes had passed.
findings.evidenceJa: 今から４０分ほど前
findings.explanation: The narration jumps back to approximately forty minutes before the present scene. 'Forty minutes had passed' states elapsed forward time instead, reversing the flashback marker.
findings.japanese: 今から４０分ほど前。
findings.todokanai: 40 minutes had passed.

findings.highlight: where the slightest thing will tick off Touma
findings.evidenceJa: 軽い気持ちで面倒くさがっている冬馬を本気で怒らせて
findings.explanation: Haruki intends to push Kazusa, who is dismissing the request as a casual nuisance, into becoming genuinely angry so the contest ends either in her joining or never speaking to him again. The English makes her anger an accidental response to 'the slightest thing,' deleting his deliberate brinkmanship.
findings.japanese:
軽い気持ちで面倒くさがっている冬馬を本気で怒らせて、
仲間になってもらうか、二度と口聞いてもらえなくなるか、
そんなギリギリの勝負をすることで。
findings.todokanai: We're down to the wire, where the slightest thing will tick off Touma, and either she'll become our ally, or she'll never talk to us again.

findings.highlight: It's because she followed the instructions in the book carefully that she was able to make something like this in practice
findings.evidenceJa: 教科書にあることがマスターできてこそ、応用が効果的に利くようになる
findings.explanation: Haruki gives a general principle: only after mastering the textbook fundamentals can one apply variations effectively, and that is where future rates of improvement diverge. The English invents a direct causal account of this meal and reduces his characteristically pedantic theory to having followed instructions carefully.
findings.japanese:
教科書にあることがマスターできてこそ、
応用が効果的に利くようになる。
つまり、ここからの上達の速さに差が出るってことで。
findings.todokanai: It's because she followed the instructions in the book carefully that she was able to make something like this in practice. She'll only get better from now on.

findings.highlight: In other words, their relationship was predestined to be turbulent because of this.
findings.evidenceJa:
つまり、二人の間には、
そんな前提条件のところから齟齬があるんだろうな。
findings.explanation: A mismatch between Setsuna and Kazusa beginning at their basic premises becomes a relationship predestined to be turbulent.
findings.japanese:
つまり、二人の間には、
そんな前提条件のところから齟齬があるんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: In other words, their relationship was predestined to be turbulent because of this.

findings.highlight: she was the one waiting for this topic to be brought up
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬のその反応を熱望していたはずの小木曽
findings.explanation: Setsuna had been longing for exactly this reaction from Kazusa—her voice finally heating up and engaging seriously—yet interrupts it. The English says she merely wanted the topic introduced, replacing the desired emotional engagement with a topical milestone.
findings.japanese:
そこに冷水を浴びせたのは、
冬馬のその反応を熱望していたはずの小木曽だった。
findings.todokanai: Ogiso puts out the flames with cold water, even though she was the one waiting for this topic to be brought up.

findings.highlight: her sulky attitude is a completely different matter, given her family's history
findings.evidenceJa: ひねくれてみせたところで、本家にはとっくにネタが上がってたりして
findings.explanation: Haruki jokes that even when he tries acting contrary, the original master of contrariness—Kazusa—has already seen through his material. The English introduces an unexplained family history and no longer expresses either his imitation or her having his number.
findings.japanese:
でも、ひねくれてみせたところで、
本家にはとっくにネタが上がってたりして。
findings.todokanai: Though her sulky attitude is a completely different matter, given her family's history.

findings.highlight: You avoid competition, you make sure no one's left behind and that everyone makes it to the end together. You don't oppose anyone, always smiling quietly.
findings.evidenceJa: 決して人とは争わず、いつも静かに笑ってる
findings.explanation: Kazusa's escalating parallel description culminates in an unmistakable adaptation of the cadence and wording of Miyazawa Kenji's Ame ni mo Makezu. The English conveys the component traits as ordinary explanatory prose but does not recreate or signal the literary echo that structures the characterization.
findings.japanese:
「非競争主義、脱落者ゼロ、一緒にゴール。
決して人とは争わず、いつも静かに笑ってる」
findings.todokanai: "You avoid competition, you make sure no one's left behind and that everyone makes it to the end together. You don't oppose anyone, always smiling quietly."

findings.highlight: that's the kind of person I've always striven to be
findings.evidenceJa: 将来的にはそういう人になりたい
findings.explanation: Haruki says that this is indeed the kind of person he would like to become in the future. The English claims it has always been his active program, reversing future aspiration into established lifelong striving immediately after Kazusa's literary caricature.
findings.japanese:
それにしても容赦のない…
確かに、将来的にはそういう人になりたいけどさぁ。
findings.todokanai: Her words are merciless… but it's true, that's the kind of person I've always striven to be.

findings.highlight: Don't try to break my train of thought.
findings.evidenceJa: そうやって足下を切り崩そうとしないの
findings.explanation: Setsuna's observation that Kazusa knows Haruki well undermines the footing of Kazusa's argument, and Kazusa tells her not to chip away at it that way. The English instead complains of an interrupted train of thought, losing Setsuna's successful counterattack and Kazusa's defensive recognition of it.
findings.japanese:
「今はあたしの話なんかしてないから。
そうやって足下を切り崩そうとしないの」
findings.todokanai: "We're not talking about me right now. Don't try to break my train of thought."

findings.highlight: Maybe you shouldn't go?
findings.evidenceJa: 行かない方がいいかしら
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother wonders whether she herself—or the family—had better not attend, because she could not bear watching Setsuna embarrass herself. The English addresses Setsuna and advises her not to participate, changing whose prospective attendance is under discussion.
findings.japanese:
「…行かない方がいいかしら？
娘が全校生徒の前で大恥かくのは見るに忍びないし…」
findings.todokanai: "…Maybe you shouldn't go? I don't want my daughter to make a complete fool of herself in front of all the students…"

findings.highlight: although I look back at the road behind, I'm unable to see that brilliant face
findings.evidenceJa: 元来た道を振り返り、俺にその整った顔を見せず
findings.explanation: Kazusa stops beside Haruki and turns back toward the road they came from, withholding her face from him. The English makes Haruki the one who looks back and merely fails to see her face, reversing the physical action and deleting Kazusa's deliberate concealment.
findings.japanese:
俺の隣を歩く歩調は、いつの間にか止まり、
元来た道を振り返り、俺にその整った顔を見せず。
findings.todokanai: She had stopped walking by my side at some point, and although I look back at the road behind, I'm unable to see that brilliant face.

findings.highlight: because I experienced that kind of drama at home in the past as well
findings.evidenceJa: 俺も、あのホームドラマにあてられていたから
findings.explanation: Haruki keeps talking because he too has been emotionally affected by the Ogiso family's home-drama-like warmth they just witnessed. The English says he continues because he experienced comparable family drama in the past, replacing the immediate emotional cause with biography.
findings.japanese:
それでも話し続けてしまうのは、
俺も、あのホームドラマにあてられていたからで。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I continue my story, because I experienced that kind of drama at home in the past as well.

findings.highlight: You're bold, Kitahara. Did you plan to convince me with your tepid attitude…? You're getting ahead of yourself.
findings.evidenceJa: 潔いな北原。そんなぬるい根性であたしを口説こうとしてたわけ？…５年早いね
findings.explanation: Kazusa sarcastically notes how readily Haruki had conceded failure, mocks the weak resolve with which he meant to win her over, and says he is five years too early. 'Bold' reverses the first evaluation, while 'getting ahead of yourself' removes the pointed five-year measure and its superiority joke.
findings.japanese:
「潔いな北原。
そんなぬるい根性であたしを口説こうとしてたわけ？
…５年早いね」
findings.todokanai: "You're bold, Kitahara. Did you plan to convince me with your tepid attitude…? You're getting ahead of yourself."

findings.highlight: which was very close to being disbanded
findings.evidenceJa: 一度空中分解した軽音楽同好会
findings.explanation: The club had actually fallen apart once and has now recovered the bare minimum form. The English says it merely came close to disbanding, softening an accomplished prior collapse into an averted possibility.
findings.japanese:
一度空中分解した軽音楽同好会は、
最低限の、本当に最低限の体裁を取り戻し、
いよいよ最後の学園祭へと突き進んでいく。
findings.todokanai: But at last, the Light Music Club, which was very close to being disbanded, has now managed to regain its form at the bare minimum and is finally pushing toward its final school festival.
